newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power firms amid colder temps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power firms amid colder temps.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the U.S. Northeast firmed Monday amid temperatures returning to winter norms and sharp upward spikes in the oil and natural gas markets.

A weekend cold front pushed out a mild weather system that brought spring-like temperatures across the region last week. Outlook for the rest of this week showed readings would peak 20-30 degrees Fahrenheit and bottom in the teens to 20s, down 10-15 degrees from a week ago.
Fuel costs to produce electricity were also lifted by the weather forecast.
Swing natural gas prices at the New York City gate climbed about 60 cents to the $4.00 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) level from Friday's $3.40.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February Henry Hub natgas futures rose 49.4 cents/mmBtu to $3.600.
NYMEX February crude futures jumped 81 cents at 26.42 per barrel, approaching the post-Gulf War high of $26.80 made December 19.
Higher crude prices usually increase costs to manufacture products such as heating oil, jet fuel and residual fuel oil, which are fuels used at fossil-fueled power plants.
Although short-term electricity prices increased, actual power demand remained soft, market sources said.
"All the (baseload) units are up. The weather is not that cold," said a New York electricity trader.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices (including transmission costs) for Tuesday delivery in the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) rose to $23.50-$25.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) from Friday's $21.00-$23.00 for Monday delivery.
Off-peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in western NYPP climbed to $15.00-$16.00 from $14.00-$15.00 Friday.
In eastern NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Tuesday climbed to $27.00-$30.00/MWh from Friday's $25.00-$26.00.
Eastern NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Tuesday were assessed in a $19.00-$22.00, up from Friday' $18.00-$20.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for day-ahead delivery at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border stayed in a $31.00-$34.00/MWh range.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery to the NU border was remained at $21.00-$23.00.
